record.title: Variant of the quantum Singleton bound for hybrid stabilizer codes
record.statement:
An $\left[\!\left[n,k\!:\!m,d\!:\!c\right]\!\right]_{q}$ hybrid stabilizer code has length $n$, quantum dimension $k$, classical dimension $m$, quantum minimum distance $d$, and classical minimum distance $c$. **Hybrid stabilizer Singleton conjecture.** Every such code satisfies

$$
k+m\leq n-2\left(d-1\right).
$$

This extends the conjectured quantum Singleton bound for arbitrary subsystem codes; the bound is known for $\mathbb{F}_{q}$-linear Clifford subsystem codes, while its validity for general subsystem and hybrid stabilizer codes remains open.
record.source_name: Andrew Nemec and Andreas Klappenecker, “Encoding Classical Information in Gauge Subsystems of Quantum Codes”, arXiv:2012.05896 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.05896

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: Diskoid representation and correspondence conjecture for abstract key polynomials
record.statement:
Let $b[?]$ be a valuation on $K[X]$ and let $Qb[?]K[X]$ be an abstract key polynomial for $b[?]$, with $b[?](Q)b[?]b[?]b[?](K^b[?])$. A **diskoid** is a subset $b[?](Q)b[?]b[?]$ whose polynomial-value minima represent the truncation along $Q$. **Diskoid representation and correspondence conjecture.** There exists a diskoid $b[?](Q)$, which is a finite union of balls, such that for every $fb[?]K[X]$ the minimum exists and satisfies

$$
b[?]_Q(f)=b[?]_{xb[?]b[?](Q)}b[?](f(x)).
$$

Moreover, there is a bijective correspondence between residually transcendental valuations over $K[X]$ that can be given by a key polynomial and the corresponding diskoids. This conjecture proposes a geometric realization of truncations and a classification of the relevant valuations by finite unions of balls.
record.source_name: Andrei Benguş-Lasnier, “Minimal Pairs, Truncations and Diskoids”, arXiv:2012.07780 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.07780

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: Asymptotic inadequacy of bounded-degree Gaussian polynomials for $\mathcal{C}^+(A)$
record.statement:
For $A>1$, let $\mathcal{C}^+(A)$ denote the relevant Fourier optimization problem, let $J_A^+(F)$ be its objective functional, and let $\mathcal{F}_n$ be the class of nonzero functions of the form $P(x)e^{-\pi x^2}$ with $P\in\mathbb{R}[x]$ of degree at most $n$. **The conjecture.** There exists an absolute $\varepsilon>0$ such that, for every integer $n\geq 1$, there exists $A_n^+>1$ for which, whenever $A\geq A_n^+$,

$$
\sup_{F\in\mathcal{F}_n}J_A^+(F)\leq\mathcal{C}^+(A)-\varepsilon.
$$

The preceding proposition proves an analogous nonpositive bound for the unsigned problem $J_A$, while numerical comparisons at $A=28$ show that bandlimited functions outperform the tested bounded-degree Gaussian-polynomial functions for the positive problem. The conjecture asserts a uniform positive gap from the optimum as $A$ becomes large.
record.source_name: Andrés Chirre and Emily Quesada-Herrera, “Fourier optimization and quadratic forms”, arXiv:2012.07781 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.07781

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: Injectivity conjecture for forgetful charts of prestable curves
record.statement:
Let $(g,n)\neq(1,0)$, and fix $d\geq 0$. For a prestable curve with $n+m$ markings, forgetting the last $m$ markings defines a morphism

$$
F_m:\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n+m}\to\mathfrak{M}_{g,n}.
$$

**Injectivity conjecture.** There exists $m_0\geq 0$ such that, for every $m\geq m_0$, the pullback

$$
F_m^*:\mathrm{CH}^d(\mathfrak{M}_{g,n})\to\mathrm{CH}^d(\overline{\mathcal{M}}_{g,n+m})
$$

is injective.

The conjecture would make the Chow groups of stable-curve moduli spaces determine the Chow groups of the corresponding prestable-curve stacks. The source notes that, for sufficiently large $m$, the image of $F_m$ is open with complement of codimension $\lfloor m/2\rfloor+1$, but injectivity of the pullback remains conjectural.
record.source_name: Younghan Bae and Johannes Schmitt, “Chow rings of stacks of prestable curves I”, arXiv:2012.09887 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.09887

Status: **open** according to the source (as of December 2020). “We have seen in Lemma that (for $m$ sufficiently large) the image of $F_m$ is open with complement of codimension $\lfloor \frac{m}{2} \rfloor +1$.”

record.title: Perfect stability conjecture for inducibility of complete partite graphs
record.statement: Let $F$ be a complete partite graph. The inducibility problem for $F$ asks for the maximum possible induced $F$-density in graphs of increasing order, and is **perfectly stable** when every graph whose induced $F$-density is close to optimal is close to an extremal construction. **Perfect stability conjecture.** The inducibility problem for $F$ is perfectly stable for every complete partite $F$. This would extend the known perfect-stability results for several small complete partite graphs; the conjecture remains open in general.
record.source_name: Hong Liu, Oleg Pikhurko, Maryam Sharifzadeh and Katherine Staden, “Stability from graph symmetrisation arguments with applications to inducibility”, arXiv:2012.10731 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.10731

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: Ashraf's signless Laplacian eigenvalue-sum conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with $n$ vertices and $e(G)$ edges, let $Q(G)$ be its signless Laplacian matrix, and let $S_k(Q(G))$ denote the sum of the $k$ largest eigenvalues of $Q(G)$. **Ashraf's conjecture.** For every $1\leq k\leq n$,

$$
S_k(Q(G))\leq e(G)+\binom{k+1}{2}.
$$

The conjecture is known for several classes, including graphs with at most ten vertices, regular graphs, trees, unicyclic graphs, bicyclic graphs, and tricyclic graphs when $k\ne3$, as well as for the specified endpoint values of $k$.
record.source_name: Zhen Lin, Lianying Miao and Shuguang Guo, “On the sum of the largest A_α-eigenvalues of graphs”, arXiv:2012.11177 (2020).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2020). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1306.0093](https://arxiv.org/abs/1306.0093).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.11177

Status: **refuted** according to the source (as of December 2020). “Gernert's conjecture was disproved by Nikiforov , who gave examples of graphs with $S_2(A(G))\geq \frac{29+\sqrt{329}}{42}n-25>1.122n-25$ and proved that $S_2(A(G))\leq \frac{2}{\sqrt{3}}n<1.155n$.”

record.title: Monotonicity and ordering conjecture for generalised Airy recurrence coefficients
record.statement:
Let $\alpha_n(t;\lambda)$ and $\beta_n(t;\lambda)$ be the recurrence coefficients appearing in the generalised Airy polynomial system, and let $t_n^*$ denote the location of the maximum of $\beta_n(t;\lambda)$. **Generalised Airy recurrence-coefficient conjecture.**

1. The recurrence coefficient $\alpha_n(t;\lambda)$ is a monotonically increasing function of $t$.
2. If $\lambda$ is fixed, then

$$
\beta_{n+1}(t;\lambda)>\beta_n(t;\lambda)
$$

for all $t$.
3. The recurrence coefficient $\beta_n(t;\lambda)$ has one maximum at $t=t_n^*$, with

$$
t_{n+1}^*>t_n^*
$$

when $\lambda$ is fixed.

These claims are suggested by plots of the recurrence coefficients for $n=1,2,\ldots,5$ and several fixed values of $\lambda$. Their general validity is not established in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Peter A. Clarkson and Kerstin Jordaan, “Generalised Airy Polynomials”, arXiv:2012.13279 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2012.13279

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of December 2020).

record.title: The polylogarithmic improvement conjecture for independent sets in omitting systems
record.statement:
Let $k\geq 3$ and $2\leq \ell<k$ satisfy $k\leq 2\ell+1$. An $(n,k,\ell)$-omitting system is an $n$-vertex $k$-uniform hypergraph with no two edges whose intersection has size $\ell$, and let $g(n,k,\ell)$ denote the minimum independence number over all such systems. **Independent-set growth conjecture.** For all fixed integers $k>\ell\geq 2$ that satisfy $k\leq 2\ell+1$, there exists a function $\omega(n)\to\infty$ as $n\to\infty$ such that

$$
g(n,k,\ell)=\Omega\left(n^{\frac{k-\ell}{k-1}}\omega(n)\right).
$$

This conjecture predicts an improvement by an unbounded factor over the known power-law scale in the range $k\leq 2\ell+1$; the paper proves the first open case $\ell=k-2$ up to a factor involving $(\log\log n)^{1/(k-1)}$, but the full assertion remains open.
record.source_name: Tom Bohman, Xizhi Liu and Dhruv Mubayi, “Independent sets in hypergraphs omitting an intersection”, arXiv:2101.04258 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.04258

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

record.title: The $K_4^-$ and $L_2$-free 3-graph Turán conjecture
record.statement:
Let $K_4^-$ be the 3-uniform hypergraph obtained from the complete 3-uniform hypergraph on four vertices by deleting one edge, and let

$$
L_2=\{123,124,125,136,456\}.
$$

For a family of forbidden 3-uniform hypergraphs, let $\operatorname{ex}(n,\mathcal{H})$ denote the maximum number of edges in an $n$-vertex 3-uniform hypergraph containing no member of $\mathcal{H}$. Let $S(n)$ be the 3-uniform hypergraph referred to in the source. **The $K_4^-$ and $L_2$-free 3-graph conjecture.**

$$
\operatorname{ex}(n,\{K_4^-,L_2\})=\frac{1}{4}\binom{n}{3}(1+o(1)).
$$

The conjecture proposes that the construction $S(n)$ has asymptotically the maximum number of edges among $\{K_4^-,L_2\}$-free 3-uniform hypergraphs. The source gives no resolution, so the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: József Balogh, Felix Christian Clemen and Bernard Lidický, “Maximum Number of Almost Similar Triangles in the Plane”, arXiv:2101.10304 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.10304

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of January 2021).

record.title: Bollobás–Scott conjecture on long cycles in Eulerian digraphs
record.statement: Let $G$ be a finite loopless directed graph, allowing both orientations of an edge, and write $d^+(v)$ and $d^-(v)$ for the outdegree and indegree of a vertex $v$. The graph is **Eulerian** if $d^+(v)=d^-(v)$ for every vertex $v$, with degree $d^+(v)=d^-(v)$ and average degree defined accordingly. **Bollobás–Scott conjecture.** If $G$ is Eulerian with average degree at least $d$, then $G$ contains a directed cycle of length at least $cd$ for some absolute constant $c>0$. This conjecture is still wide open: the best general lower bound mentioned in the paper is $(d^{1/2})$, with stronger bounds under additional maximum-degree assumptions, and the conjecture remains open even for simple graphs.
record.source_name: Oliver Janzer, Benny Sudakov and István Tomon, “Long directed paths in Eulerian digraphs”, arXiv:2101.11601 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2101.11601

Status: **open** according to the source (as of January 2021). “The difficulty of this conjecture is perhaps reflected by the fact that it is open even for simple graphs.”

record.title: The diamond-poset grid density conjecture
record.statement:
Let $D_2$ denote the diamond poset, and for $d\geq2$ let $\pi_{d,D_2}$ and $\pi^*_{d,D_2}$ be its weak and strong density parameters in the $d$-dimensional grid. **The diamond-poset density conjecture.** For every $d\geq2$,

$$
\pi_{d,D_2}=\pi^*_{d,D_2}=2+\frac{1}{d}.
$$

The paper identifies $D_2$ as the smallest poset for which the Boolean density conjecture has not been verified and gives the two-dimensional value, while the formula for larger dimensions remains conjectural.
record.source_name: Dániel Gerbner, Dániel T. Nagy, Balázs Patkós and Máté Vizer, “Forbidden subposet problems in the grid”, arXiv:2102.08297 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.08297

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of February 2021).

record.title: Bilinear forms graph smallest eigenvalue conjecture
record.statement:
Let $H_q(d,e)$ be the bilinear forms scheme on the $d\times e$ matrices over $\mathbb{F}_q$, where $d\leq e$. In its distance-$j$ graph, write $B_j(i)$ for the eigenvalue indexed by $i$, with $0\leq i,j\leq d$.

**Bilinear forms eigenvalue conjecture.** For $q\geq 3$, or $q=2$ and $d\neq e$, $B_j(d-j+1)$ is the smallest eigenvalue in the distance-$j$ graph for $1\leq j\leq d$.

The conjecture was previously proved for $q\geq 4$ and is proved in this paper for all $q\geq 2$, so the claim is now resolved.
record.source_name: Sebastian M. Cioabă and Himanshu Gupta, “On the eigenvalues of Grassmann graphs, Bilinear forms graphs and Hermitian forms graphs”, arXiv:2102.10155 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2102.10155

Status: **open** according to the source (as of February 2021). “The following conjecture was also posed in (see Conjecture 2.11) and is still open.”

record.title: A conjectured upper bound for the iterated Mycielski L(2,1)-labeling number
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph of order $n\geq 1$ with maximum degree $\bigtriangleup$, and let $M^t(G)$ denote the $t$-fold iterated Mycielski graph of $G$, where $t\geq 1$. Let $\lambda(H)$ denote the $L(2,1)$-labeling number of a graph $H$.

**Iterated Mycielski labeling conjecture.** For all $t\geq 1$,

$$
\lambda(M^t(G))\leq (2^t-1)(n+1)+\bigtriangleup^2.
$$

This is proposed as a weaker form of the general $\bigtriangleup^2$-conjecture, using upper bounds for the $L(2,1)$-labeling number of Mycielski and iterated Mycielski graphs. Its resolution is not specified in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Kamal Dliou, Hicham El Boujaoui and Mustapha Kchikech, “L(2,1)-Labeling of the iterated Mycielski of graphs and some related to matching problems”, arXiv:2103.00341 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.00341

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of March 2021). “This conjecture was proven to be true by Havet et al. for graphs with a large maximum degree.”

record.title: Borradaile et al.'s lexicographic optimality conjecture for SC-Path-Reversal
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple undirected graph admitting a strongly connected orientation. An orientation of $G$ assigns a direction to every edge; among strongly connected orientations, compare the indegrees in lexicographic order. SC-Path-Reversal starts from an arbitrary strongly connected orientation and repeatedly reverses a strongly reversible directed path, namely a path from $u$ to $v$ with $d^-(u)<d^-(v)-1$ such that $u$ two-reaches $v$ by two arc-disjoint directed paths.

**Borradaile et al.'s conjecture.** The algorithm SC-Path-Reversal finds a strongly connected orientation that minimizes the lexicographic order of indegrees.

The algorithm is known to run in polynomial time and to minimize the maximum indegree. The conjecture concerns the stronger lexicographic objective.
record.source_name: Hongyu Zhou and Xinmin Hou, “Strongly connected orientation with minimum lexicographic order of indegrees”, arXiv:2103.01017 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.01017

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

record.title: Positive random-subgraph independence-gap conjecture
record.statement:
For a graph $G$, let $\bar{\alpha}(G)$ be the maximum uniform measure of an independent set. Let $\alpha^*(G)$ be the largest expected normalized size of an independent set found inside a positively correlated random union of vertex parts, and define

$$
\epsilon^*(\alpha)=\inf_{G:\,\bar{\alpha}(G)\geq\alpha}\left\{\bar{\alpha}(G)-\alpha^*(G)\right\}.
$$

**Positive random-subgraph independence-gap conjecture.** $\epsilon^*(\alpha)>0$ for all $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$. This conjecture is proposed as a general statement about independent sets in random subgraphs; the paper explains that it would imply decay of normalized independence numbers for Hamming powers of the Kneser graph and thus Levine's conjecture.
record.source_name: Ehud Friedgut, Gil Kalai and Guy Kindler, “The success probability in Lionel Levine's hat problem is strictly decreasing with the number of players, and this is related to interesting questions regarding Hamming powers of Kneser graphs and independent sets in random subgraphs”, arXiv:2103.01541 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.01541

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

record.title: The strong four-vertex tournament conjecture
record.statement:
Let $\accentset{\leftrightarrow}{K}_2$ be the complete digraph on two vertices, let $S_2^+$ be the two-out-star, and let $\vec{K}_4^s$ be the unique strong tournament on four vertices. For a family of forbidden induced digraphs, write $\operatorname{Forb}_{\operatorname{ind}}(\cdot)$ for the corresponding class and $\vec{\chi}$ for dichromatic number. **Strong four-vertex tournament conjecture.** 
$$
\vec{\chi}(\operatorname{Forb}_{\operatorname{ind}}(\accentset{\leftrightarrow}{K}_2,S_2^+,\vec{K}_4^s))=3.
$$
 This is presented as the smallest open case of the broader question whether $\{\accentset{\leftrightarrow}{K}_2,S_2^+,H\}$ is heroic for every hero $H$; the authors state that a new method may be required.
record.source_name: Raphael Steiner, “On coloring digraphs with forbidden induced subgraphs”, arXiv:2103.04191 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.04191

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2021).

record.title: The linear expected-face conjecture for simple graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph on $n$ vertices, and choose an orientable embedding of $G$ uniformly at random. Write $F_G$ for the number of faces of the resulting embedding. **Linear expected-face conjecture.** For every such graph $G$, the expected number of faces is

$$
\mathbb{E}[F_G]=O(n).
$$

The paper establishes logarithmic upper bounds and gives linear lower-bound constructions, but does not find a family with superlinear expected numbers of faces; the conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Jesse Campion Loth, Kevin Halasz, Tomáš Masařík, Bojan Mohar and Robert Šámal, “Random 2-cell embeddings of multistars”, arXiv:2103.05036 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.05036

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

record.title: The linear expected-face conjecture for multigraphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a multigraph on $n$ vertices, and let $\mu$ be its maximum edge-multiplicity. Choose an orientable embedding of $G$ uniformly at random. **Linear multigraph expected-face conjecture.** The expected number of faces is

$$
O\bigl(n\log(2\mu)\bigr).
$$

This adjusts the simple-graph conjecture to account for parallel edges. The paper presents it after proving bounds for simple graphs and does not establish it in full; its status is open.
record.source_name: Jesse Campion Loth, Kevin Halasz, Tomáš Masařík, Bojan Mohar and Robert Šámal, “Random 2-cell embeddings of multistars”, arXiv:2103.05036 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.05036

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

record.title: Friedgut–Kalai–Kindler packing conjecture for maximum independent sets
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph on $n$ vertices, and let $\tau>0$ and $k$ be parameters. A maximum independent set is an independent set of size $\alpha(G)$.

**Friedgut–Kalai–Kindler conjecture.** For every $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$ there exist $k$ and $\tau>0$ such that, if $G$ has a maximum independent set of size $\alpha n$, then there are pairwise disjoint vertex subsets $A_1,A_2,\ldots,A_r$ such that

$$
|A_i|=k\quad\text{for all }i,
$$

$$
\left|\bigcup_{i=1}^r A_i\right|\geq \tau n,
$$

and every maximum independent set in $G$ intersects every $A_i$.

The paper states that this conjecture is false for every fixed $\alpha\in(0,1/2)$, even when the requirement on the union is omitted; it does hold for $\alpha>1/2$ by Hajnal's theorem.
record.source_name: Noga Alon, “Hitting all maximum independent sets”, arXiv:2103.05998 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.05998

Status: the source reports no resolution (as of March 2021); treated as **open**. (An automated reading suggested “refuted”, which the source does not establish — worth checking against the literature.)

record.title: Häggkvist's transversal cycle-factor conjecture for blow-ups of cycles
record.statement:
Let $C_k$ be the cycle on $k$ vertices, and let the **$n$-blow-up** of $C_k$ be the graph with vertex parts $V_1,\dots,V_k$, each of size $n$, where consecutive parts are joined according to the edges of $C_k$. For a spanning subgraph $G$ of this blow-up, write $\delta^*(G)$ for its minimum degree between consecutive vertex parts. A **transversal $C_k$-factor** is a collection of $n$ vertex-disjoint copies of $C_k$, each containing one vertex from every part.

**Häggkvist's conjecture.** For every $k\geq 3$, if

$$
\delta^*(G)\geq \left(1+\frac{1}{k}\right)\frac{n}{2}+1,
$$

then $G$ has a transversal $C_k$-factor.

The conjecture is tight when $k=3$, while the example described in the source shows that for $k\geq4$ the degree threshold cannot be decreased by more than $1$.
record.source_name: Beka Ergemlidze and Theodore Molla, “Transversal C_k-factors in subgraphs of the balanced blow-up of C_k”, arXiv:2103.09745 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.09745

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of March 2021).

record.title: The cubic edge diameter conjecture for maximum degree
record.statement:
Let $h_t(\Delta)$ be the smallest integer such that every graph with $h_t(\Delta)$ edges and maximum degree at most $\Delta$ contains two edges whose distance is at least $t$; equivalently, $h_t(\Delta)-1$ is the largest number of edges in a graph of maximum degree at most $\Delta$ whose line graph has diameter at most $t$. Here $h_3(\Delta)$ denotes the case $t=3$.

**Cubic edge diameter conjecture.**

$$
h_3(\Delta)\leq \Delta^3-\Delta^2+\Delta+2,
$$

with equality if $\Delta$ is one more than a prime power.

The bound is motivated by point-line incidence graphs of finite projective planes, which attain $\Delta^3-\Delta^2+\Delta$ edges before a one-edge subdivision. The conjecture has been confirmed for $\Delta=3$, where $h_3(3)=23$, but remains open in general.
record.source_name: Stijn Cambie, Wouter Cames van Batenburg, Rémi de Joannis de Verclos and Ross J. Kang, “Maximising line subgraphs of diameter at most t”, arXiv:2103.11898 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2103.11898

Status: **open** according to the source (as of March 2021). “For all other values of $t$ the conjecture remains open.”

record.title: Isomorphism of minimum-eigenvector-induced Gilbert graphs
record.statement:
Let $G_t$ be the graph obtained at step $t$ of the construction, with vertex set $V_t$. For each vector $v$, let $a^{(t)}_v$ be the eigenvector of $G_t$ with eigenvalue $lambda_{min}^{(t)}$. **Minimum-eigenvector-induced graph conjecture.** For all vectors $v$ such that $a^{(t)}_v$ is the eigenvector with eigenvalue $lambda_{min}^{(t)}$ in $G_t$, the graphs induced by

$$
\{u\in V_t\mid\langle u,v\rangle=0\}
$$

are isomorphic. This claim concerns the independence of the induced graph from the choice of a minimum-eigenvalue eigenvector in the proposed graph-spectral coding construction; the supplied text does not state whether it has been proved or disproved.
record.source_name: Zicheng Ye, Huazi Zhang, Rong Li, Jun Wang, Guiying Yan and Zhiming Ma, “Improving the Gilbert-Varshamov Bound by Graph Spectral Method”, arXiv:2104.01403 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.01403

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2021). “Section concludes the results and gives some open problems.”

record.title: Haemers's Laplacian eigenvalue conjecture for graph toughness
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a simple graph with minimum degree $\delta$. Let $\mu_2$ and $\mu_n$ denote the second-smallest and largest eigenvalues of the Laplacian matrix of $G$, respectively, and let $t(G)$ be its toughness. **Haemers's conjecture.**

$$
t(G)\geq\frac{\mu_2}{\mu_n-\delta}.
$$

The source attributes this conjecture to Haemers and presents it as a proposed lower bound for the toughness of arbitrary graphs in terms of Laplacian eigenvalues. The supplied material does not state whether it has been resolved.
record.source_name: Xiaofeng Gu and Willem H. Haemers, “Graph toughness from Laplacian eigenvalues”, arXiv:2104.03845 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.03845

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

record.title: Outerplanar graph star chromatic index conjecture
record.statement:
Let $G$ be an outerplanar graph with maximum degree $\Delta\ge 4$, and let $\chi'_{\mathrm{star}}(G)$ denote its star chromatic index, the smallest number of colors in a proper edge coloring with no bichromatic path or cycle of length four.

**Outerplanar graph star chromatic index conjecture.** Every such graph satisfies

$$
\chi'_{\mathrm{star}}(G)\le \left\lfloor\frac{3\Delta}{2}\right\rfloor+1.
$$

Known bounds give $\chi'_{\mathrm{star}}(G)\le \left\lfloor\frac{3\Delta}{2}\right\rfloor+12$, with the additive constant reducible to $9$ by more involved analysis. The conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: Zhengke Miao, Yimin Song, Tao Wang and Xiaowei Yu, “List star edge coloring of generalized Halin graphs”, arXiv:2104.05958 (2021).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2011–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1105.1906](https://arxiv.org/abs/1105.1906).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.05958

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2021).

record.title: Spectral extremal graphs conjecture for Turán graphs plus $O(1)$ edges
record.statement:
Let $F$ be a graph, and let $\mathrm{EX}(n,F)$ denote the family of $F$-extremal graphs on $n$ vertices. Suppose that the graphs in this family are Turán graphs plus $O(1)$ edges. Let $\mathrm{SPEX}(n,F)$ denote the family of $F$-free graphs on $n$ vertices with maximum spectral radius.

**General spectral extremal conjecture.** For sufficiently large $n$,

$$
\mathrm{SPEX}(n,F) \subset \mathrm{EX}(n,F).
$$

The conjecture proposes that, whenever the ordinary extremal graphs differ from the relevant Turán graphs by only constantly many edges, the spectral extremal graphs have the same structure. The paper establishes this phenomenon for the no-odd-wheel setting for all $k\notin\{4,5\}$ and sufficiently large $n$, while the cases $k\in\{4,5\}$ remain a technical obstacle.
record.source_name: Sebastian Cioabă, Dheer Noal Desai and Michael Tait, “The spectral radius of graphs with no odd wheels”, arXiv:2104.07729 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.07729

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

record.title: The minimal length conjecture for finite-projective-dimension modules
record.statement:
Let $(R,\mathfrak m)$ be a local ring, let $e(R)$ denote its Hilbert–Samuel multiplicity, and let $\ell_R M$ denote the length of an $R$-module $M$. **Minimal length conjecture.** For every nonzero $R$-module $M$ of finite projective dimension,

$$
\ell_R M\geq e(R).
$$

This conjecture concerns the smallest possible length of a nonzero module of finite projective dimension. It implies Lech's conjecture at least for Cohen–Macaulay rings, but remains open in the stated generality.
record.source_name: Srikanth B. Iyengar, Linquan Ma and Mark E. Walker, “Multiplicities and Betti numbers in local algebra via lim Ulrich points”, arXiv:2104.10140 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.10140

Status: **open** according to the source (as of April 2021). “One measure of its difficulty is that it implies the still open Lech's conjecture , recalled in Section , at least for Cohen-Macaulay rings; see .”

record.title: Projective-geometric correspondence conjecture for WDVV systems
record.statement: A WDVV system is a system of first-order PDEs considered together with its projective-geometric structures. A **quadratic line complex** is the associated family of lines in projective space defined by a quadratic condition, and a **linear line congruence** is a family of lines defined linearly in the relevant Plücker coordinates. **Projective-geometric correspondence conjecture.** To every WDVV system there are associated a quadratic line complex and a linear line congruence. In the known cases, projective reciprocal transformations exhibit these structures and make the bi-Hamiltonian WDVV hierarchy a projective-geometric object; their existence for every WDVV system remains open.
record.source_name: Jakub Vašíček and Raffaele Vitolo, “WDVV equations and invariant bi-Hamiltonian formalism”, arXiv:2104.13206 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2104.13206

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of April 2021).

record.title: The logarithmic cycle-packing bound for inversion number
record.statement:
For an oriented graph $D$, let $\nu(D)$ be its cycle packing number, the maximum number of pairwise vertex-disjoint directed cycles. Let $g$ be the minimum function such that $\operatorname{inv}(D)\leq g(\nu(D))$ for every oriented graph $D$.

**Logarithmic cycle-packing conjecture.** For all $k$, $g(k)=O(k\log k)$; equivalently, there is an absolute constant $C$ such that

$$
\operatorname{inv}(D)\leq C\cdot\nu(D)\log(\nu(D))
$$

for every oriented graph $D$.
The conjecture would give a substantially better growth bound than the very large bound obtained through the known relation between cycle transversals and cycle packings.
record.source_name: Jørgen Bang-Jensen, Jonas Costa Ferreira da Silva and Frédéric Havet, “On the inversion number of oriented graphs”, arXiv:2105.04137 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.04137

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

record.title: The regularity formula for squarefree powers of edge ideals of forests
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a forest. For a positive integer $k$, let $I(G)^{[k]}$ denote the $k$th squarefree power of the edge ideal of $G$, let $\operatorname{reg}$ denote Castelnuovo–Mumford regularity, let $\operatorname{aim}(G,k)$ denote the maximum cardinality of an induced $k$-matching of $G$, and let $\operatorname{mat}(G)$ denote the matching number of $G$.

**Forest regularity conjecture.** For every $1\leq k\leq \operatorname{mat}(G)$,

$$
\operatorname{reg}(I(G)^{[k]})= \operatorname{aim}(G,k)+k.
$$

The conjecture proposes that the upper bound established for squarefree powers of edge ideals of forests is always sharp. It is motivated by the preceding results and Macaulay2 computations, but the source provides no resolution.
record.source_name: Nursel Erey and Takayuki Hibi, “Squarefree powers of edge ideals of forests”, arXiv:2105.09744 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.09744

record.title: Rall's complete-factor conjecture for well-dominated Cartesian products
record.statement:
Let $G$ and $H$ be nontrivial connected graphs, and let $G\Box H$ denote their Cartesian product. A graph is **well-dominated** if every minimal dominating set is a minimum dominating set.

**Rall's conjecture.** If $G\Box H$ is well-dominated, then at least one of $G$ or $H$ is a complete graph.

This conjecture is the explicit final formulation of the proposed classification of connected well-dominated Cartesian products. The paper proves the corresponding characterization when one factor is complete, but the assertion for arbitrary connected factors remains open.
record.source_name: Douglas F. Rall, “On well-dominated direct, Cartesian and strong product graphs”, arXiv:2105.09797 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.09797

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

record.title: Conjecture that every extremal graph is complete multipartite
record.statement: Let $\bm{k}=(k_1,\hspace{0.9pt}.\hspace{0.3pt}.\hspace{0.3pt}.\hspace{1.5pt},k_s)$ be a non-increasing sequence of natural numbers, and let a graph be $\bm{k}$-extremal if it attains the maximum number $F(n;\bm{k})$ of $\bm{k}$-valid edge-colourings among graphs on $n$ vertices. A graph is **complete multipartite** if its vertex set can be partitioned into parts such that every pair of vertices in distinct parts is adjacent. **Extremal multipartite conjecture.** For every $\bm{k}$, every $\bm{k}$-extremal graph is complete multipartite. At least one extremal graph is known to be complete multipartite, but the conjecture asserts this for every extremal graph.
record.source_name: Oleg Pikhurko and Katherine Staden, “Stability for the Erdős-Rothschild problem”, arXiv:2105.09991 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.09991

record.title: Rainbow Hajnal--Szemerédi conjecture for graph systems
record.statement:
Let $t$ and $n$ be positive integers, and let $\textbf{G}=\{G_1,G_2,\ldots,G_{\frac{n}{t}\binom{t}{2}}\}$ be an $n$-vertex graph system. **Rainbow Hajnal--Szemerédi conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(G_i)\geq\left(1-\frac{1}{t}\right)n
$$

for every $i\in\left[\frac{n}{t}\binom{t}{2}\right]$, then $\textbf{G}$ admits a rainbow $K_t$-factor.
This is the exact rainbow analogue of the Hajnal--Szemerédi theorem: the conjecture asks whether the sharp minimum-degree threshold remains sufficient when each clique edge must be selected from a distinct graph in the system.
record.source_name: Yangyang Cheng, Jie Han, Bin Wang and Guanghui Wang, “Rainbow spanning structures in graph and hypergraph systems”, arXiv:2105.10219 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.10219

record.title: The explicit formula conjecture for the monochromatic subset-sum constant
record.statement:
Let $r\geq 3$ be an integer, and let $c_r$ be the constant studied for monochromatic subset sums. Let $b_0$ be the unique root with $b_0>1$ of

$$
b^r-2rb+r-1=0.
$$

**Explicit formula conjecture.** For every integer $r\geq 3$,

$$
c_r=\left(1-\frac{1}{2b_0}\right)\left(1+\frac{1}{2rb_0-r}\right).
$$

This gives the proposed exact value of $c_r$ and makes precise the claim that the previously obtained upper bound is tight for three or more colors. Its resolution is not supplied in the excerpt.
record.source_name: David Conlon, Jacob Fox and Huy Tuan Pham, “The upper logarithmic density of monochromatic subset sums”, arXiv:2105.15195 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.15195

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of May 2021).

record.title: Big ends eventually periodic conjecture
record.statement:
Let $mathbb T_q$ be the tautological tree, whose ends determine sequences of $ell$-values and associated $F$-sequences. An end is **big** when

$$
\sum \frac{1}{\ell(n)}<\infty,
$$

and it is of **type $S$** when its associated $F$-sequence satisfies

$$
F(m+1)=F(m)+1
$$

for all sufficiently large $m$. **Big ends eventually periodic conjecture.** Every big end is of type $S$. The conjecture proposes that the summability condition defining big ends forces eventual type-$S$ behavior of the associated combinatorial sequence; its status is not resolved in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Danny Calegari, “Combinatorics of the Tautological Lamination”, arXiv:2106.00578 (2024).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.00578

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

record.title: Differential equations for the exponential generating functions of two vincular avoidance classes
record.statement:
Let $[\Pi]$ be a set of possibly vincular patterns, and define its exponential generating function by

$$
E[\Pi]=\sum_{n\ge 0} \#\operatorname{Av}_n[\Pi]\frac{x^n}{n!}.
$$

Write $\overline{123}$ and $\overline{213}$ for the two vincular patterns in question, and let $E'=\frac{dE}{dx}$.

**Conjectures.** For $E=E[\overline{123}]$ and for $E=E[\overline{213}]$, respectively,

$$
E'=E^2-E+1,
$$

and

$$
E'=e^{E-\frac{x^2}{2}}.
$$

These differential equations would determine the corresponding avoidance-class enumerations, since their explicit solutions can be found by separation of variables once the equations are proved. The source provides no resolution of either conjecture.
record.source_name: Rachel Domagalski, Jinting Liang, Quinn Minnich, Bruce E. Sagan, Jamie Schmidt and Alexander Sietsema, “Cyclic Pattern Containment and Avoidance”, arXiv:2106.02534 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.02534

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

record.title: Conjecture on Zeckendorf sum-of-digits maximum order complexity along polynomial subsequences
record.statement:
Let $s_Z(n)$ denote the sum of digits of $n$ in Zeckendorf base, let $\mathcal{S}_Z=(s_Z(n)\bmod 2)_n$, and let $\mathcal{S}_{Z,P}$ be the sequence obtained by restricting $\mathcal{S}_Z$ to a polynomial subsequence $P(n)$, where $P$ has degree $d\geq2$. Write $M(\mathcal{S}_{Z,P},N)$ for its maximum order complexity up to length $N$. **Zeckendorf polynomial-subsequence conjecture.** There are constants $c,C>0$ such that, for all sufficiently large $N$,

$$
cN^{1/(2d)}\leq M(\mathcal{S}_{Z,P},N)\leq CN^{1/(2d)}.
$$

Equivalently, $M(\mathcal{S}_{Z,P},N)\asymp N^{1/(2d)}$. The paper proves the corresponding lower bound, so the conjecture asserts its sharpness; computational evidence is given for squares.
record.source_name: Damien Jamet, Pierre Popoli and Thomas Stoll, “Maximum order complexity of the sum of digits function in Zeckendorf base and polynomial subsequences”, arXiv:2106.09959 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.09959

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

record.title: Minimum degree conjecture for perfect clique tilings in multipartite graphs
record.statement:
Let $k\geq r\geq 2$ and $\gamma>0$. Let $G$ be a $k$-partite graph on $n$ vertices with parts $V_1,\ldots,V_k$ such that $|V_i|\leq n/r$ for every $i$. For each $i\in [k]$, write $\delta(V_i)$ for the minimum degree of a vertex in $V_i$. **Multipartite perfect $K_r$-tiling conjecture.** If

$$
\delta(V_i)\geq \left(1-\frac{1}{2r}+\gamma\right)n-|V_i|
$$

for all $i\in [k]$, then $G$ has a perfect $K_r$-tiling.

This conjecture proposes a sufficient minimum total-degree condition for perfect $K_r$-tilings in unbalanced multipartite graphs and is asymptotically necessary in certain cases. It is presented as an open direction beyond known balanced results, including the asymptotically best possible balanced multipartite threshold proved by Lo and Sanhueza-Matamala.
record.source_name: Louis DeBiasio, Ryan Martin and Theodore Molla, “Powers of Hamiltonian cycles in multipartite graphs”, arXiv:2106.11223 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.11223

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of June 2021).

record.title: Tree packing conjecture for families of trees
record.statement: Let $n\in\mathbb{N}$, and let $(T_s)_{s\in[n]}$ be a family of trees such that $v(T_s)=s$ for every $s\in[n]$. **Tree packing conjecture.** The family $(T_s)_{s\in[n]}$ packs into the complete graph $K_n$. The paper presents this as one of the central tree-packing conjectures and later proves it for sufficiently large $n$ when the trees have maximum degree $O(n/\log n)$; the general case with large-degree vertices remains open.
record.source_name: Peter Allen, Julia Böttcher, Dennis Clemens, Jan Hladký, Diana Piguet and Anusch Taraz, “The tree packing conjecture for trees of almost linear maximum degree”, arXiv:2106.11720 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2106.11720

Status: **solved** according to the source (as of June 2021). “The first general result on this conjecture was proved in .”

record.title: Conjecture on second-largest denominators in Egyptian fraction representations of 1
record.statement:
An Egyptian fraction representation of $1$ is a representation of the form

$$
1=\frac{1}{a_1}+\frac{1}{a_2}+\cdots+\frac{1}{a_k}
$$

with positive integers as denominators. An integer $d$ is the **second-largest denominator** when it is the second-largest member of the denominator set in such a representation. **Second-largest denominator conjecture.** Every integer $d\ge 5$ can be the second-largest denominator in an Egyptian fraction representation of $1$. This conjecture is motivated by Erdős's questions about the density of integers that cannot occur as denominators of specified ranks; the source reports that every sufficiently large integer is known to occur as the second-largest denominator, while the assertion for every $d\ge5$ remains open.
record.source_name: Greg Martin and Yue Shi, “An algorithm for Egyptian fraction representations with restricted denominators”, arXiv:2107.05076 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.05076

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

record.title: Sum-diameter conjecture for paths
record.statement:
Let $P_n$ denote the path graph on $n$ vertices. The **sum-diameter** of a graph $G$, denoted $\operatorname{sd}(G)$, is the minimum range of a labeling whose induced sum graph is $G$.

**Sum-diameter conjecture for paths.** For $n\geq 3$, we have

$$
\operatorname{sd}(P_n)=\begin{cases} 2n-3 & 3\leq n\leq 6,\\ 2n-2 & n\geq 7.
\end{cases}
$$

An exhaustive computer search verifies the values through $n=13$, but the asserted formula beyond the computed range remains open. The conjecture refines the preceding bounds for the sum-diameter of paths.
record.source_name: Rupert Li, “The Spum and Sum-diameter of Graphs: Labelings of Sum Graphs”, arXiv:2107.09025 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.09025

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

record.title: The conjecture on arbitrarily large topological four-genus of algebraically slice GA-knots
record.statement:
A **GA-knot** is a knot that can be written as a connected sum of algebraic knots and their reverse mirror images. A knot is **algebraically slice** if it bounds a genus-zero surface in a suitable algebraic concordance sense, and its **topological four-genus** is the minimum genus of a locally flat surface it bounds in the topological four-ball.

**Arbitrarily large four-genus conjecture.** There are algebraically slice GA-knots with arbitrary large topological four-genus.

The conjecture asks whether the known examples of algebraically slice, non-slice GA-knots, whose topological four-genus is one, can be extended to examples with no universal bound on their topological four-genus.
record.source_name: Maria Marchwicka and Wojciech Politarczyk, “On the slice genus of generalized algebraic knots”, arXiv:2107.11299 (2023).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.11299

record.title: Bilu–Linial conjecture for arbitrary graphs
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a graph with maximum degree $\Delta(G)>1$. An **edge-signing** of $G$ is a map from $E(G)$ to $\{-1,1\}$; write $G^\sigma$ for the resulting edge-signed graph and let $\rho(G^\sigma)$ be the maximum absolute value of an eigenvalue of its signed adjacency matrix. **Bilu–Linial conjecture for arbitrary graphs.** There exists an edge-signing $\sigma$ of $G$ such that

$$
\rho(G^\sigma)\leq 2\sqrt{\Delta(G)-1}.
$$

This is presented as a stronger conjecture obtained by omitting regularity from the regular-graph formulation, and is attributed to reference `greg`. The source gives no resolution status.
record.source_name: Mohsen Alinejad and Sanaz Fulad, “Equitable partitions for Ramanajun graphs”, arXiv:2107.11563 (2021).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2013–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:1907.04349](https://arxiv.org/abs/1907.04349), [arXiv:1311.3268](https://arxiv.org/abs/1311.3268).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.11563

record.title: Minimum-size unavoidable subsets of cyclic permutations
record.statement:
Let $\overline{S_k}$ denote the set of cyclic permutations of length $k$, and let an **unavoidable subset** be a subset that every sufficiently long permutation contains as a vincular pattern. The sets from the preceding theorem have cardinality

$$
(k-1)!.
$$

**Minimum-cardinality conjecture.** For all $k \geq 1$, the minimum cardinality of an unavoidable subset of $\overline{S_k}$ is

$$
(k-1)!.
$$

The conjecture asserts that the explicitly constructed sets are the most efficient unavoidable subsets. It follows the established construction of unavoidable sets of cardinality $(k-1)!$; the claim that no smaller unavoidable subset exists remains unresolved in the supplied text.
record.source_name: Rupert Li, “Vincular Pattern Avoidance on Cyclic Permutations”, arXiv:2107.12353 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.12353

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of July 2021).

record.title: Heim–Neuhauser conjecture for D’Arcais polynomials
record.statement:
Let $P_0(x)=1$ and, for $n\geq 1$, define the D’Arcais polynomials by

$$
P_n(x):=\frac{x}{n}\sum_{j=1}^n\sigma(j)P_{n-j}(x),\qquad \sigma(j):=\sum_{d\mid j}d.
$$

For integers $a>b\geq 0$, define

$$
\Delta_{a,b}(x):=P_{a-1}(x)P_{b+1}(x)-P_a(x)P_b(x).
$$

**Heim–Neuhauser conjecture.** For all $x\geq 2$,

$$
\Delta_{a,b}(x)\geq 0,
$$

except for $b=0$ and $(a,b)=(6,4)$. The inequality remains true for $x\geq 3$ when $b=0$, and for $x\geq x_{6,4}$ when $(a,b)=(6,4)$, where $x_{a,b}$ is the largest real root of $\Delta_{a,b}(x)$. This conjecture extends the colored-partition inequality to D’Arcais polynomials; the source does not provide a resolution status.
record.source_name: Bernhard Heim and Markus Neuhauseer, “Proof of the Bessenrodt–Ono inequality by Induction”, arXiv:2108.00191 (2021).
record.references:
**2 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2020–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2011.11056](https://arxiv.org/abs/2011.11056).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.00191

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

record.title: Zhuang–Gao conjecture on the Gao constant
record.statement:
Let $G$ be a finite group. Write ${\sf d}(G)$ for the smallest integer such that every sequence over $G$ of length at least ${\sf d}(G)+1$ has a nonempty product-one subsequence, and write ${\sf E}(G)$ for the smallest integer such that every sequence over $G$ of length at least ${\sf E}(G)$ has a product-one subsequence of length $|G|$. **Zhuang–Gao conjecture.** For every finite group $G$,

$$
{\sf E}(G)={\sf d}(G)+|G|.
$$

The inequality ${\sf E}(G)\geq {\sf d}(G)+|G|$ is known in general, while equality is established for several families of groups. The conjecture remains open in the generality stated in the supplied source.
record.source_name: Fabio Enrique Brochero Martínez, Abílio Lemos, B. K. Moriya and Sávio Ribas, “The main zero-sum constants over D_2n C_2”, arXiv:2108.00823 (2021).
record.references:
**3 papers in this index state this conjecture** (2017–2021). The statement above is taken from the most recent of them; the others are [arXiv:2107.06969](https://arxiv.org/abs/2107.06969), [arXiv:1707.03639](https://arxiv.org/abs/1707.03639).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.00823

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

record.title: The bounded-degree wall or line-graph induced-subgraph conjecture
record.statement: Let $W_{k\times k}$ be the $(k\times k)$-wall, let $L(H)$ denote the line graph of $H$, and let $\Delta(G)$ and $\operatorname{tw}(G)$ denote the maximum degree and treewidth of a graph $G$, respectively. A **subdivision** of $W_{k\times k}$ is obtained by subdividing edges of the wall. **Bounded-degree wall or line-graph conjecture.** For every $\Delta>0$ there is a function $f_{\Delta}:\mathbb{N}\rightarrow\mathbb{N}$ such that every graph $G$ with $\Delta(G)\leq\Delta$ and $\operatorname{tw}(G)\geq f_{\Delta}(k)$ contains a subdivision of $W_{k\times k}$ or the line graph of a subdivision of $W_{k\times k}$ as an induced subgraph. This is the bounded-maximum-degree affirmative answer proposed for the converse concerning useful families; the supplied text states that it remains open.
record.source_name: Tara Abrishami, Maria Chudnovsky, Cemil Dibek, Sepehr Hajebi, Paweł Rzążewski, Sophie Spirkl and Kristina Vušković, “Induced subgraphs and tree decompositions II. Toward walls and their line graphs in graphs of bounded degree”, arXiv:2108.01162 (2023).

Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.01162

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

record.title: Grinblat's conjecture on rainbow matchings in $(n,v)$-multigraphs
record.statement:
An **$(n,v)$-multigraph** is an $n$-edge-coloured multigraph in which the edges of each colour span a disjoint union of non-trivial cliques whose total number of vertices is at least $v$. Let $v(n)$ be the minimum integer $v$ such that every $(n,v)$-multigraph contains a rainbow matching of size $n$. **Grinblat's conjecture.** For all $n\geq 4$, 
$$
v(n)=3n-2.
$$
 This problem generalises rainbow matching questions such as the bipartite Aharoni–Berger conjecture and arose from Grinblat's study of algebras of sets; the conjecture remains open here.
record.source_name: David Munhá Correia, Alexey Pokrovskiy and Benny Sudakov, “Short proofs of rainbow matching results”, arXiv:2108.07734 (2021).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.07734

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of August 2021).

record.title: The exact linear bound conjecture for few-angle point sets
record.statement:
Let $P(k)$ denote the minimum number of distinct angles determined by a finite set of points in the plane whose cardinality is at least $k$.

**Exact linear bound conjecture.** The lower bound on $P(k)$ in Theorem is tight. Namely,

$$
P(2k)=2k+3\quad\text{and}\quad P(2k+1)=2k+3
$$

for all $k\geq 1$.

The conjecture proposes exact values for $P(k)$ in every parity class, strengthening the currently established lower bound. It concerns planar point sets; investigating $P(k)$ for point sets in more than two dimensions remains an open problem.
record.source_name: Henry L. Fleischmann, Steven J. Miller, Eyvindur A. Palsson, Ethan Pesikoff and Charles Wolf, “Optimal Point Sets Determining Few Distinct Angles”, arXiv:2108.12034 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.12034

Status: **open** according to the source (as of August 2021). “It is also an open problem to investigate $P(k)$ with point sets in more than two dimensions.”

record.title: Uniform lower-bound conjecture for the Schwarz preconditioner
record.statement:
Let $A$ be the discretized integral operator in the referenced two- or three-dimensional models, and let $T^{-1}_{\text{Schwarz}}$ be the Schwarz preconditioner associated with the specified overlapping domain decomposition. **Uniform lower-bound conjecture.** The smallest eigenvalue satisfies

$$
\lambda_{\min}(T^{-1}_{\text{Schwarz}} A) \ge C > 0,
$$

where $C$ is a positive constant. This conjecture asserts that the Schwarz preconditioner remains uniformly effective as the discretization is refined; the supplied text gives numerical motivation but no resolution.
record.source_name: Chao Chen and George Biros, “Overlapping Domain Decomposition Preconditioner for Integral Equations”, arXiv:2108.12574 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2108.12574

record.title: Berkovich's conjecture on non-inner automorphisms of finite p-groups
record.statement:
Let $p$ be a prime number and let $G$ be a finite nonabelian $p$-group. An automorphism of $G$ is **non-inner** if it is not induced by conjugation by an element of $G$.

**Berkovich's conjecture.** Every finite nonabelian $p$-group admits a non-inner automorphism of order $p$.

This conjecture concerns the existence of automorphisms of the smallest possible nontrivial prime order outside the inner automorphism group. The paper proves it for finite $p$-groups of coclass $4$ and $5$ when $p\geq 5$, and for an additional class of odd-order nonabelian $p$-groups with cyclic center; the general conjecture remains open.
record.source_name: P. Komma, “Non-inner automorphisms of order p in finite p-groups of coclass 4 and coclass 5”, arXiv:2109.00335 (2022).
record.references:
Source: https://arxiv.org/abs/2109.00335

Status: no resolution is reported in the source (as of September 2021).
